clue.text: Vehicle carrying exceptionally great load, for example

indicators.note: a vehicle carrying something holds it inside, so the other letters go within the vehicle's

parts.note: a tram is a vehicle running on rails in a street

indicators.note: exceptionally hints at something out of the ordinary, so the letters of great are put in an unusual order

parts.note: taken as written, as anagram fodder

explanation.surface: A tram hauling an unusually heavy cargo, given as an example.
explanation.walkthrough: 'load, for example' is not freight: the word LOAD itself, having four letters, is the example of what is defined.
explanation.definitionFit: A tetragram is any word of four letters, and LOAD is one instance of such a word.

clue.text: Tracking device worn by English sailor that gets into hot water

indicators.note: worn by means attached around, so the device's letters wrap round the other letters

parts.note: an electronic tag tracks the wearer's movements
AB, able-bodied seaman, is a sailor

explanation.surface: An English sailor wearing an electronic tag who keeps getting into trouble.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Gets into hot water' looks like an idiom for trouble but is literal: you drop one into a cup of boiling water.
explanation.definitionFit: A tea bag is literally steeped in a cup of boiling water to brew the drink.

clue.text: Parody about head of state becomes successful

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the parody's letters go round the extra letter

parts.note: a take-off is a mocking imitation

indicators.note: the head of a word is its first letter

parts.note: its first letter is S

explanation.surface: A satire about the leader of a country turns out to be a hit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'head of state' looks like a president, but it is only the first letter of the word state.
explanation.definitionFit: When a venture takes off it suddenly starts to do well, an idiom for succeeding.

clue.text: A good primate's religious feasts

parts.note: an ape is a primate; with the possessive its letters are apes

explanation.surface: A well-behaved monkey's sacred banquets.
explanation.walkthrough: The apostrophe in primate's is ignored, a common convention. Agapes were early Christian love feasts.
explanation.definitionFit: An agape is a love feast, a communal meal held by early Christians as a religious gathering.

clue.text: Sensationalist paper embarrassed the Crown?

parts.note: someone embarrassed goes red in the face
the crown of the head is its top; the question mark flags the misleading capital

explanation.surface: A tabloid humiliated the monarchy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the Crown' looks like the monarchy, but it is the top of the head. A red top is a British tabloid, so called from its red masthead.
explanation.definitionFit: Red tops are British tabloids like The Sun, known for lurid, sensational stories.

clue.text: Composer of religious service with belief primarily lacking

parts.note: Mass is the Catholic service of the Eucharist

indicators.note: primarily lacking means missing its first letter

parts.note: a tenet is a principle or belief

explanation.surface: A composer of church music who has lost his faith at the outset.
explanation.walkthrough: Jules Massenet was a French composer of operas such as Manon.
explanation.definitionFit: Jules Massenet was a nineteenth-century French composer best known for operas like Manon and Werther.

clue.text: Man of words, I understand, shortened script finally

indicators.note: shortened tells us to cut the final letter off the radio word

parts.note: in radio talk 'Roger' means message received and understood

indicators.note: finally points to the closing letter of the word script

parts.note: its last letter is T

explanation.surface: A wordsmith acknowledging that a script has at last been cut down.
explanation.walkthrough: Radio operators say this word for 'message received'. Peter Mark Roget compiled the famous thesaurus.
explanation.definitionFit: Roget compiled the best-known English thesaurus, so he is the archetypal collector of vocabulary.

clue.text: Soldiers, having sounded hypocritical, expressed a change of mind

parts.note: RE, the Royal Engineers, is a regiment of the British Army
to cant is to talk with sanctimonious insincerity

explanation.surface: Troops who had spoken insincerely announced they had thought again.
explanation.walkthrough: RE is the usual crossword abbreviation for the Royal Engineers.
explanation.definitionFit: To recant is to withdraw a former opinion publicly, so the person has announced a new view.

clue.text: Pleasant army officer, one substituting for Queen

indicators.note: substituting for means one thing takes another's place in the word

parts.note: a general is a senior army officer
ER, Elizabeth Regina, stands for the Queen
one is I, the Roman numeral

explanation.surface: A friendly officer standing in for the monarch.
explanation.walkthrough: In GENERAL, swap the ER for I.
explanation.definitionFit: Genial means friendly and cheerful in manner, a close synonym for pleasant company.

clue.text: Groan maybe going round pub — a problem with background noise

indicators.note: going round means encircling, so the name's letters surround the pub's

parts.note: Titus Groan is the hero of Mervyn Peake's Gormenghast novels, so Titus is an example of a Groan
an inn is a pub

explanation.surface: A grumble circling the bar, a nuisance amid the din.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Groan' looks like a moan but is a surname: Titus Groan is the hero of Mervyn Peake's Gormenghast books.
explanation.definitionFit: Tinnitus is a medical condition of persistent ringing or buzzing in the ears, a constant background sound.

clue.text: Uneasy, having aggressive advocate for Cockney region of city

indicators.note: Cockney speech famously drops the H at the start of words, so the opening H goes

parts.note: a hawk is someone who argues for a warlike policy
a ward is an electoral division of a city

explanation.surface: Someone feels uncomfortable because a combative campaigner is speaking up for an East End district.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for Cockney' tells us to say the word as a Cockney would, dropping its H: HAWK becomes AWK. A Cockney is a working-class Londoner from the East End.
explanation.definitionFit: Feeling awkward means being uncomfortable or embarrassed, the same as being uneasy.

clue.text: Wild beasts in land I've associated with Satanism, wrongly

indicators.note: wrongly says the letters are put together in the wrong order and must be rearranged

parts.note: taken as written, as anagram fodder
taken as written, as anagram fodder

explanation.surface: Fierce animals in a country somehow mixed up with devil worship.
explanation.walkthrough: The fifteen letters of LAND I'VE and SATANISM rearrange to give both lights of the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Tasmanian devils are fierce carnivorous marsupials living wild on the island of Tasmania.

clue.text: Town has attractive appearance with river flowing round

parts.note: gloss is a shiny, attractive surface look

indicators.note: flowing round suggests the river turning back on itself, so its letters are read backwards

parts.note: the Po is the great river of northern Italy

explanation.surface: A town looks handsome and has a river curling about it.
explanation.walkthrough: The Po is Italy's longest river. Glossop is a market town in Derbyshire, in the English Peak District.
explanation.definitionFit: Glossop is a real market town in Derbyshire, so the bare word town is a plain category definition.

clue.text: Short message not on outside of the box

indicators.note: placed on the outside of something means wrapping round it, so these letters enclose the others

parts.note: taken as written
the box is British slang for television, and telly or tele is another word for it

explanation.surface: A brief note that refuses to fit outside the container.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The box' is everyday British slang for the television.
explanation.definitionFit: A notelet is a small folded card or sheet for writing a brief letter or memo.

clue.text: Compassion evident in Sophy and Stephen?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: kindness and pity for others
second, cryptic meaning: the centre letter of each name is P, the musical abbreviation for piano, meaning soft; so both names are soft at heart

explanation.walkthrough: Read the answer as SOFT-HEARTED-NESS: the middle letter of both SOPHY and STEPHEN is P, which in music means piano, or soft. So the two names have soft hearts.
explanation.definitionFit: Being soft-hearted means being tender and easily moved to pity, which is what compassion is.

clue.text: With such impassivity, man may turn to monasticism

indicators.note: turn to signals that letters are reworked into another word, here the answer with man becoming the longer word

parts.note: taken as written, as anagram fodder
taken as written; these letters are the ones added to the answer

explanation.surface: Calmly enduring all, a fellow might take up the monastic life.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer's letters plus M, A and N rearrange to MONASTICISM; so take MAN out of MONASTICISM and rearrange.
explanation.definitionFit: Stoicism is endurance of hardship without showing feeling, an unmoved calm like impassivity.

clue.text: Somehow relishes having a problem with a will?

definitions.text: having a problem with a will?

indicators.note: somehow suggests something done in an unknown way, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written, as anagram fodder

explanation.surface: Somebody enjoys being stubborn.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a problem with a will' looks like stubbornness, but the will is a testament: with nobody to inherit, it has a problem.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone heirless has no one to inherit, which leaves their last testament without an obvious beneficiary.

clue.text: Plant an avens — rodent will invade it

parts.note: an is the indefinite article, giving A

indicators.note: invade means enter, so the rodent's letters go inside

parts.note: Geum is the botanical genus of the avens
a rat is a rodent

explanation.surface: Gardeners' plant warning: a rat will get into the flowers.
explanation.walkthrough: The avens belongs to the genus Geum, and the clue uses the Latin genus name rather than a common synonym.
explanation.definitionFit: Ageratum is a garden flower, the floss flower, with fluffy blue clusters, so it is a plant.

clue.text: Retinue that is turning up to protect queen and boy at match

indicators.note: protecting means surrounding, so the reversed letters go round the queen's
in a down clue turning up means read from the bottom upwards, so the letters go backwards

parts.note: ie, id est, means that is
a page boy attends the bride at a wedding, a match

explanation.surface: An entourage that turns out to guard the queen and a lad at the game.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Match' looks like sport but is a marriage, where a page boy attends the bride.
explanation.definitionFit: An equipage is a carriage with its attendants, the train of servants accompanying a dignitary.

clue.text: Where car may be hit at cricket field

definitions.meaning: first meaning: parked on the drive outside a house
second meaning: the ..., a straight shot played to the leg side of the field

explanation.walkthrough: Split as ON DRIVE, the phrase gives where you leave the car at home, and also the cricket stroke driven through the on (leg) side.
explanation.definitionFit: A parked car sits on the drive, and the on drive is a recognised batting stroke in cricket.

clue.text: See 10
More than one Spaniard enjoys the sun, we hear

indicators.note: we hear tells us the word is judged by its sound, not its spelling

parts.note: to bask is to lie enjoying warmth and sunlight

explanation.surface: Many Spaniards like to lie in the sunshine, so people say.
explanation.walkthrough: BASKS and BASQUES sound alike. The Basques live in northern Spain and south-west France.
explanation.definitionFit: The Basques are a people of northern Spain, so several of them are a group of Spaniards.

clue.text: German location mostly generated soldiers

indicators.note: mostly means all but the final letter

parts.note: bred means produced or generated
men are soldiers, as in officers and men

explanation.surface: A place in Germany mainly produced troops.
explanation.walkthrough: BRED loses its last letter to give BRE, then MEN.
explanation.definitionFit: Bremen is a city and state in northern Germany, so it is a German place.

clue.text: Batty sort of woman in the home counties, perhaps a foreign lady?

parts.note: SE, the south-east of England, contains the home counties around London
Nora Batty is the formidable woman in the British sitcom Last of the Summer Wine

explanation.surface: A dotty woman in the area around London might be someone from abroad.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Batty' looks like crazy but is a surname: Nora Batty of the long-running TV comedy Last of the Summer Wine. The home counties are the counties around London, in the SE.
explanation.definitionFit: Señora is the Spanish title for a married woman, the equivalent of Mrs or madam.

clue.text: Hard to endure energy cut at first

indicators.note: at first says the word for cut is placed at the front

parts.note: to sever is to cut
E is the physics symbol for energy

explanation.surface: Losing power at the outset is tough to bear.
explanation.walkthrough: 'at first' tells you SEVER goes in front, before the E.
explanation.definitionFit: Severe hardship or pain is intense and harsh, so it is difficult to bear.

clue.text: Parade around avenue trapping a boy getting caught inside

parts.note: c or ca, short for circa, means around a date

indicators.note: trapping means holding something within, so the avenue's letters surround the rest

parts.note: Ave is the street-sign abbreviation for avenue

indicators.note: inside says the letter for caught goes within the boy's letters

parts.note: a lad is a boy
C is the cricket scorecard abbreviation for caught

explanation.surface: A procession circles the avenue and catches a youngster who gets arrested.
explanation.walkthrough: 'around' is circa, abbreviated C, placed first rather than an instruction to wrap; the caught C goes inside the boy and the avenue traps a plus the boy.
explanation.definitionFit: A cavalcade is a procession, originally of riders, so it is a formal parade.

clue.text: Parking space? About time!

indicators.note: about here means turned round, so the letters are read in the opposite order

parts.note: room means space, as in room to move
an age is a period of time

explanation.surface: An exasperated driver finally finds somewhere to park: about time!
explanation.walkthrough: 'About time!' reads as an exclamation of relief, but it is wordplay. 'Parking' is the definition: a boat is parked by mooring it.
explanation.definitionFit: Moorage is the place or act of mooring a vessel, the boating counterpart of a parking spot.

clue.text: Religious leader may appear in places of worship, no question

indicators.note: no here means without, so the letters for question are taken away

parts.note: mosques are places of worship for Muslims

explanation.surface: A churchman may turn up in temples, and no one doubts it.
explanation.walkthrough: Remove QU from MOSQUES to leave the prophet's name.
explanation.definitionFit: Moses led the Israelites out of Egypt and received the Ten Commandments, a founding religious figure.

clue.text: Insane game getting rid of one disruptive element

indicators.note: getting rid of says a letter is discarded from the pool before it is rearranged
disruptive means throwing into disorder, so the remaining letters are jumbled

parts.note: taken as written, as anagram fodder
one is I, the Roman numeral

explanation.surface: A crazy game that loses one troublesome player.
explanation.walkthrough: Take the I out of INSANE GAME and rearrange the nine letters left.
explanation.definitionFit: Manganese is a chemical element, a hard grey metal with atomic number 25.
